messages:
Mia Chen: Heads-up — we need to finalize the modular-pack boundaries for the sprint. core ask: unbundle compute credits from QoS addons so customers can buy throughput/SLA separately. goal: minimize churn for existing commit customers while offering clear upsell path.
Jordan Patel: +1. Sales feedback: most deals want predictable throughput (commit + burst). customers hate per-route knobs. can we keep packaging simple: Base + Performance Addon + Priority Lane? :thinking_face: @Devin thoughts?
Devin Ortega: Proposed pack shape: Base (model access, basic rate limits), Performance Addon (reserved throughput, burst reservoir), Priority Lane (latency p95 SLA, routing priority, faster autoscale). limits: softfloor for every commit (we guarantee baseline), hard cap for burst.
Samira Khan: Partner note — resellers want a monthly line-item for addons (easier to bundle). AcmeHealth pilot asked for dedicated priority lane + on-prem commit at a discount. we should support a negotiated multiplier/discount in contract templates.
Lexi Rivera (Legal): Legal constraints to keep in mind: 1) SLA credits need a liability cap (do not surface open-ended credit terms), 2) cannot change pack economics mid-contract without 60d notice and opt-out for customers, 3) reseller discounts must be reflected in the SOW and can't be backdated.
pricing-bot: quick sim (very rough):
```
Base: $0.0008/token
Performance Addon: +$X/hr per reserved vGPU equivalent
Priority Lane: +20% on unit price or +$Y/mo per route
Estimated impact: 8-14% revenue uplift, 10-18% gross margin delta depending on workload mix
```
Jordan Patel: Sales preference = simple monthly addon pricing for resellers. Usage-based for self-serve, fixed addon for enterprise. keeps quoting simple.
Devin Ortega: Open question: billing model for Priority Lane — invoice monthly fixed fee vs per-request surcharge. tradeoffs: fixed = easier to sell, per-use = more accurate economics and avoids overcommit.
Samira Khan: For pilots, prefer fixed monthly so customers can budget. we'll trade predictability for some margin.
Lexi Rivera (Legal): Contract terms: add clause "No retroactive pricing adjustments for active commitments" + a negotiated change-control path. Also add a cap on aggregate SLA credits per month (e.g., max 10% of monthly committed fees).
Mia Chen: Launch criteria proposal — pilot with 3 customers (1 reseller, 1 enterprise, 1 self-serve):
- KPI: P95 latency for Priority Lane < 200ms
- KPI: Cost delta for typical chatbot workload < 15% vs baseline
- KPI: Sales convert pilot -> paid in < 90 days or provide feedback loop
- Ops: automated metrics and alerting in console, rollout playbook
Jordan Patel: Timeline idea: internal pilot next 2 weeks, customer pilots week 3-6, canary week 7, GA week 9-10.
Devin Ortega: Implementation notes: need router policy changes, quota service updates, and billing SKU additions. will open infra tickets after this thread.
Samira Khan: Action for sales: compile 3 pilot customers + target commercial terms this week.
Lexi Rivera (Legal): I'll draft the contract language for SLA caps and change-control. need pricing ranges from product for exact thresholds.
Mia Chen: Action items summarized:
- Devin: infra + billing tickets + SKU draft (owner, due EOW)
- Jordan/Samira: pilot customer list + commercial terms (due 3 days)
- Lexi: contract clauses draft (due 4 days)
- Pricing-bot / Product: run 3 workload sims with suggested numbers and share sensitivity table (due EOW)
Thanks all — let's reconvene after artifacts. :thumbsup:
